principles: Verifier-owned evidence, not prompts or callers, decides rollout eligibility.
Rollout changes blocking only after measured proof; diagnostic semantics remain invariant.
Rollback is non-destructive and preserves signed history.
Full 3x2 identity and adapter completeness fail closed.
drivers: Prevent another late REVIEW omission class without weakening independent review.
Keep adoption bounded to the existing flat project policy.
Expose user-visible metrics and stable failure reasons.

options.name: A: Signed rollout report plus explicit flat opt-in
B: Automatically promote after telemetry accumulation

chosen: A: Signed rollout report plus explicit flat opt-in
rationale: Choose an explicit verifier-owned report whose exact signed receipt is consumed by the flat project enforcement gate. It proves measured thresholds without auto-flipping configuration, preserves identical diagnostics across observe/warn/enforce, and supports rollback by changing blocking policy only while retaining all evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Caller fabricates a passing cohort or edits aggregate metrics
preMortem.trigger: Report accepts caller verdicts or unbound aggregates
preMortem.mitigation: Derive metrics from registered cohort case records, sign/hash the report and reproduce the projection; reject caller status and mismatched aggregates.

preMortem.trigger: Host labels are not bound to signed quorum evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Require current full-3x2 receipt with three rounds and two supported providers; stable code for degraded/missing host.

preMortem.scenario: Fewer review rounds are bought with waivers or weaker checks
preMortem.mitigation: Require zero positive waiver delta, unchanged check inventory and 100 percent supported seeded omission detection.

preMortem.scenario: Rollback destroys evidence or changes diagnostic truth
preMortem.consequence: Audit history is lost and status becomes mode-dependent
preMortem.mitigation: Rollback changes only config blocking mode; report remains immutable/readable and diagnostics are mode invariant.
Only registered supported adapter profiles can qualify; disagreement/blind spots yield partial or unsupported and fail promotion.
